title: Chicken Marsala
subtitle: Pan-fried chicken breast with Marsala and mushroom sauce
excerpt: Chicken Marsala is a thinly pounded chicken breast pan-fried and finished in a sauce of Marsala wine, mushrooms, and butter. It's quick enough for a weeknight and the sauce, which comes together while the chicken rests in the pan, is really good.
sourceNotes: Chicken Marsala is an Italian-American dish developed in the United States using the Sicilian fortified wine Marsala. The preparation is similar to scaloppine al Marsala from Italian cooking, transposed to chicken breast.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made ahead and reheated gently. Fry the chicken fresh.

content.text: Chicken Marsala is a weeknight pan sauce dish: thinly flattened chicken breast, dredged in flour and fried golden, then finished in the same pan with Marsala wine, mushrooms, and butter. The whole thing takes 25 minutes. The sauce is made from what's left in the pan after frying, which is the only technique you need to know.

items.prepNote: butterflied or pounded to 1 cm thickness

content.text: Place the {{chicken-breast}} cutlets between two sheets of cling film and pound to a uniform 1 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper. Dust both sides in {{plain-flour}}, shaking off any excess.

Heat {{olive-oil}} and half the {{unsalted-butter}} in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. When the butter foams, add the chicken in a single layer. Cook for three to four minutes per side until golden. Remove to a warm plate.

In the same pan over medium-high heat, add the {{chestnut-mushrooms}} and cook for four to five minutes until browned and their liquid has evaporated. Add {{garlic}} and {{thyme-fresh}} and cook for one minute.
Pour in {{fortified-marsala}} and scrape up the browned bits from the base. Let it bubble for two minutes. Add {{chicken-stock}} and simmer for five minutes until the sauce has reduced by half.

Take off the heat and stir in the cold {{unsalted-butter}} in small pieces: this enriches the sauce and gives it a slight sheen. Taste and season. Return the chicken to the pan and spoon the sauce over the top. Scatter with {{parsley-flat}}.

items.cause: Sweet Marsala rather than dry, or too much reduction.
items.fix: Use dry Marsala if possible. If using sweet Marsala, balance with a squeeze of lemon and a little more stock.

items.symptom: The flour coating falls off during frying
items.cause: Not dried properly before dredging, or pan not hot enough.
items.fix: Pat the chicken completely dry. The pan needs to be hot enough that the chicken sizzles immediately on contact. Don't move the chicken for the first two minutes.

items.symptom: The mushrooms are wet and pale instead of browned
items.cause: Pan not hot enough or too many mushrooms crowding the pan.
items.fix: The moisture from the mushrooms needs to evaporate before browning can happen. Fry in a single layer over high heat and don't stir for the first two minutes.

Simmer for another two to three minutes. The sauce should cling lightly to the back of a spoon. If it's still very thin, mix a teaspoon of flour into a tablespoon of cold water and stir it in, then simmer for two more minutes.

content.text: Chicken Marsala is the American version of scaloppine al Marsala, a Sicilian pan sauce dish made with veal. Italian immigrants found veal expensive in America. Chicken breast became the substitute, and the dish became a staple of Italian-American restaurant menus. Serve with pasta, polenta, or mashed potato to catch the sauce.
